still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.

The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels, and the April 2032 liraglutide 6–11 label still requires six-monthly growth checks, Tanner staging and eating-disorder screening, with no age restriction.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 32.6% ever-used − 21.8% current = 10.8% of adults who used and are off now. About 55% of current users are on a second or later course (12.0 pts), and 2.4 pts cycled and are off again, so (12.0 + 2.4) / 32.6 ≈ 44% of ever-users have cycled. The other 8.4 pts stopped once and have not restarted. First-course current users are 9.8 pts, and 9.8 + 12.0 + 2.4 + 8.4 = 32.6. This fits one-year persistence of ~33% on cash weekly and oral products, ~40% inside the Medicare verified-adherence protocol and ~60% on clinic MariTide, with 36–47% restarting within a year. Age check: 0.20×11.5 + 0.33×20.5 + 0.24×30.5 + 0.23×23.5 = 2.3 + 6.8 + 7.3 + 5.4 ≈ 21.8. Income thirds average ~21.8. Users: 21.8% of ~274M adults ≈ 59.7M. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare ~16.5M (27.6%), Medicaid ~7.0M (11.7%), so public payers cover ~23.5M (39.3%) and are now the largest payer category. Commercial is ~13.0M (21.8%). Legitimate cash (TrumpRx, direct, telehealth) is ~16.8M (28.1%), including ~1.0M on calm plans and ~0.5M on cash AUD plans. Imported or counterfeit product is ~6.4M (10.7%), down from 7.5M as Medicaid AUD and obesity coverage absorbed part of the bottom third. Sum 59.7M. 65+ check: ~63M adults 65+ × 23.5% ≈ 14.8M, plus ~1.7M disabled under-65 Medicare users ≈ 16.5M. About 1.2M Medicare obesity-route starters lost coverage at the six-month checkpoint in 2034. Most went to cash or the gray market, or stopped and joined the off-now population. Adult obesity is ~32.6%. About 21% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in non-expansion-state low-income adults under 65 and the rural South. Pediatric: ~1.3% of under-18s are on a drug, ~2.9% of 12–17s, with teen oral starts up after normalisation, and ~0.2% of 6–11s. About 4.9M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. CMS's April 2033 Part D final rule reinterprets the statutory weight-loss exclusion so it no longer covers chronic obesity treatment. From January 2034 it covers anti-obesity medication for BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with a listed comorbidity, behind prior authorisation and a verified-adherence protocol. Coverage continues only with proportion-of-days-covered ≥80% from plan fill data plus connected-scale weights at months 6 and 12 showing ≥5% loss or maintenance. Baseline DXA is required for women 65+ and men 70+. Medicare users ~16.5M: ~11.0M on the pre-existing diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, ~5.0M on the new obesity route, ~0.5M with AUD as the primary code. Gross Part D incretin spend: 11.0M × $230 × 12 ≈ $30.4B, plus 5.0M × $195 × 12 ≈ $11.7B, plus 0.5M × $190 × 12 ≈ $1.1B, for ≈ $43.2B a year, up from ~$31.6B. Medicaid: AUD is a medically accepted indication, so oral semaglutide for AUD is a covered outpatient drug in every state. States may require prior authorisation and counselling enrolment but not BMI. Obesity coverage is in 13 states, up from 7; 11 of them use the CMS verified-adherence protocol to get the rule's enhanced administrative match. Medicaid users ~7.0M (~3.0M diabetes, ~1.2M AUD, ~2.8M obesity): 7.0M × ~$150 net after rebates × 12 ≈ $12.6B.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $4–30 a month across 100+ brands, and generic oral semaglutide tablets are now made in India for African and Southeast Asian tenders. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials sell for $20–55 in markets without enforceable patents. Canadian and Brazilian generics run CAD 45–80 and BRL 170–280. India and China supply roughly two-thirds of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline continued. TrumpRx maintenance prices: Wegovy pill 25 mg $179, the new Wegovy pill 50 mg $229, Foundayo $139–199, injectable Wegovy and Zepbound $229–279. MariTide direct cash is $229. Starting oral doses stay at $149. Retatrutide is ~$379 cash direct, and amycretin is still mostly on commercial formularies behind prior authorisation. Employer coverage fell from 30% to 28%, as some firms pointed retirees and pre-retirees toward Medicare. Monitored metabolic tracks hold ~6.0M enrollees inside the ~13.0M commercial users, ~4.1M of them on clinic MariTide (4.9M MariTide users in total). Orals are ~57% of users, up from 46%. The Wegovy pill 50 mg's head-to-head label moved new starts off needles, and Medicare formularies default to orals. The gray market shrank to ~6.4M but remains significant: Telegram and WhatsApp resellers, cloned-serial pens, and now counterfeit 50 mg tablets.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg and 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide, approved Jan 2033; ASAM and APA guidelines list it as a first-line option alongside naltrexone)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; growth-monitoring label)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide); the non-CVD 60+ extension is still off-label pending the confirmatory trial
mainstream_offlabel_uses: dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD; some of it moved onto the Medicare obesity route where BMI qualifies
'calm' and 'focus' low-dose plans, ~1.0M subscribers and shrinking as platforms reposition toward on-label AUD
'drug holidays' and weekend dose-skipping, now routinely advised by clinicians
semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity (off-label, low)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity comes from an existing product in a new form, not a new molecule. Novo filed an sNDA in Mar 2033 for the Wegovy pill 50 mg, backed by a 72-week head-to-head non-inferiority trial against injectable Wegovy 2.4 mg (~15.5% vs ~15.8% weight loss). It was approved Mar 2034 with a comparative-efficacy statement, the first pill labelled as equivalent to an injection. No oral matches tirzepatide or retratutide. Oral amycretin read out phase 3 in mid-2034 at ~19% and has not been filed; it will not reach the market before 2036. The oral semaglutide AUD sNDA (filed Jan 2032) was approved Jan 2033. The tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial read out in late 2034 and is being analysed; no resubmission has been made yet. The bimagrumab-type muscle adjunct filed Jul 2032 got a CRL in 2033 asking for fracture-outcome data, so it is not approved. Implant programmes remain in phase 2 and are not on the market. Global incretin market ~$185B (2033). US net prices drift down 3–5% a year and brands hold above ~$150.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic tracks. GI tolerability of the 50 mg pill is similar to the injection. Chronic diarrhoea in long-term users is routinely worked up for EPI.
Elevated with rapid weight loss. The absolute count is rising with Medicare obesity-route volume.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation centres on EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; EPI MDL ongoing, with bellwether trials set for 2035.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare cohort hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles, with no new data. Exposure is broadening as ~5M obesity-route beneficiaries start, many of them women over 70.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained. CMS's 2034 protocol requires baseline DXA for women 65+ and men 70+. The muscle-adjunct CRL (2033) cited missing fracture outcomes.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults or in AUD trial populations, despite high baseline psychiatric comorbidity.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA's Sentinel postmarketing observational study (Nov 2033) reproduced the existing pattern: clinically meaningful anhedonia ~7–8% vs ~3% in controls, ~10% on retatrutide, dose-related. At calm-plan doses the excess was small and imprecise. There is still no randomised evidence. Brief interruptions are widely reported to restore pleasure within days, which feeds the drug-holiday practice.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA called the data insufficient for causal labelling and added 'mood changes' to patient counselling materials only. No warning was added.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. People removed from coverage at Medicare checkpoints are now a visible regain cohort.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly. It underpins the chronic-therapy framing and the adherence protocols.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users, and a particular concern in older beneficiaries with small appetites. Low ferritin is reported in adolescent girls.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language on labels; CMS protocol includes it in the 12-month check.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years) is unchanged. No new data changed the estimate. The 2033 disclosure that Novo had held an internal 2027 extension-study analysis showing falling faecal elastase is about when the company knew, not about the size of the risk. Tirzepatide's excess is still small and non-significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label unchanged since Mar 2031. FDA issued a warning letter to Novo (Dec 2033) over postmarketing reporting under 21 CFR 314.80. A DOJ civil investigation is open.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. No new long-horizon signal. Cycling effects on bone and pancreas are still poorly characterised, and the drug-holiday practice adds a new, unstudied intermittent pattern.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; no new requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~30,000 by late 2034. Smaller regional clusters occurred, with no event on the 2031 scale. Counterfeit 50 mg tablets appeared within months of the launch. Poison-centre calls have stabilised at ~5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts maintained. CBP seizures are flat at 2031–32 levels. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak, and no statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: No new data beyond the 2032 interim analysis (~0.7 cm/year height-velocity deficit in prepubertal starters) and the Swedish registry (ARFID HR ~1.8). The next PMR analysis is due 2035, and final adult height is still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label monitoring language unchanged. The EMA review concluded in 2033 with similar monitoring wording and no age restriction. AAP lifestyle-first interim guidance stands.

food_and_beverage.state: About 39% of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~11–13% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~10%. The Medicare rule moved the new losses into 65+ shoppers: breakfast cereal, baked goods and cookies in Florida and Arizona retirement markets fell fastest in 2034. Kroger and Publix added 'pill-friendly' small-portion and protein sections near the pharmacy. Store-by-zip planning is now standard, and value packs persist in low-coverage zips.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~16% from 2025 and beer ~10%. The AUD approval moved the hardest-hit segment from heavy drinkers in insured suburbs to heavy drinkers everywhere, because Medicaid must cover it. The Kentucky bourbon glut worsened: two Bardstown-area distilleries mothballed production lines, and barrel brokers report record unsold inventory. On-premise bar closures continue in the Midwest. Non-alcoholic products grow but stay below ~3% of category value.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Senior-heavy markets lost early-bird and buffet volume in 2034. Chains like Cracker Barrel and Golden Corral are testing half-plate pricing in Florida. Portion-tiered menus are universal in casual dining. QSR value menus remain strong in low-coverage areas.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists are still shrinking. Mature-women's brands are recutting size runs downward. Resale and stretch serve cyclers and people disenrolled at Medicare checkpoints. Growth is in structured athletic wear and alterations.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Medicare Advantage plans market resistance-training classes beside the DXA requirement, and SilverSneakers-type programmes report record strength-class enrolment. Premium DXA-plus-coaching runs $250–400 a month. Employer tracks still bundle InBody scans with the clinic shot.

insurance.state: Part D gross incretin spend is ~$43B a year. The 2035 Part D base beneficiary premium was announced up ~9%, partly on obesity-route volume, and CMS used demonstration authority to cap stand-alone plan increases. Employer coverage is 28%, and self-insured firms with older workforces encourage 65+ workers onto Medicare. Adherence differentials are now common in mid-sized self-insured plans. Medicaid budgets in the 13 obesity-coverage states show incretins as a top-three drug line.

pharma.state: Novo's shares fell ~25% after the September 2033 document release. Its CEO left in Oct 2033, and a DOJ civil investigation is open. Volume still grew because Medicare formularies default to oral semaglutide at the negotiated price and the 50 mg pill launched in Mar 2034. Lilly gained commercial share. Amgen holds employer tracks. Indian and Chinese makers dominate volume outside the US.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug is unremarkable, so the body now signals which stage you are at, not whether you take it. The morning pill beside the coffee is the new household fixture. A lean, muscled body still reads as coached and covered. A soft-thin older body reads as Medicare. Visible regain reads as a checkpoint failure, a bad batch or a choice, and people expect an explanation for it.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Class sorting persists but has shifted toward age and payer. In The Villages, Florida, the Medicare rule made the pill at breakfast nearly universal among eligible residents within a year, and pickleball-club gossip now concerns who failed the six-month weigh-in. In Charlotte and Austin, 'off-drug lean' remains the elite boast. In Memphis and the Mississippi Delta, Medicaid obesity coverage arrived only in Mississippi's neighbours, so the cycler body persists. Louisville residents on Kentucky Medicaid can get the pill for drinking but not for weight.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter. Hosts plan 'holiday' dinners around guests' skipped doses: a wedding, Thanksgiving or a birthday is when people are expected to be off for the weekend and hungry again. Bread Alone claims ~700 congregations. School debates centre on teen pill use at lunch.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps let users tag 'on', 'holidaying' or 'off', and the 'off' tag draws questions. Couples coordinate drug holidays for anniversaries and trips. Lean-mass badges have lost novelty.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has become something people schedule: muted on weekdays and allowed back on holidays. Being off without a reason (cost, coverage, a bad batch) is read as a decision that needs defending. Unmuted reframed itself around 'the right to be off' and campaigns against Medicare checkpoints. MAHA remains focused on children, and fat-acceptance groups stay apart from both.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The Sentinel study (Nov 2033) reproduced ~7–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia vs ~3% in controls, ~10% on retatrutide, dose-related. With ~60M users, that excess is roughly 2.5–3M people. A much larger group, perhaps a third of users in consumer surveys, reports milder flatness and treats it with dose step-downs or 'holidays' of 2–4 days. Calm-plan subscriptions fell from ~1.3M to ~1.0M as the evenness became something people complained about rather than paid for.
interior_life.framing: Mostly a side effect people manage, like caffeine jitters. Clinicians write 'dose holiday' instructions, and late-night comedy calls it 'the beige'. Telehealth platforms dropped 'calm you can schedule' for on-label AUD language. HR no longer says 'steadiness'. Unmuted calls the checkpoint rules 'mandatory flatness'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Adherence verification and holidays collide. Weekday-only dosing pushes the proportion of days covered under 80%, so prescribers now write formal step-down or interruption orders, which CMS accepted as a protocol exception code in Aug 2034. Employer-track MariTide enrollees cannot take a holiday from a monthly clinic shot, and Columbus-corridor workers complain they get no flexibility. Calm and focus are no longer listed on résumés.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday' became a genre: songs and short films set on the weekend the pill stops. 'Off' memoir is mainstream. Streaming 'ambient' recommendations for calm-plan subscribers drew a consumer-protection complaint. Sportsbook handle per account stays down in covered suburbs.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples schedule holidays together. Sex therapists report 'holiday-only intimacy' as a common pattern. Mismatches arise when only one partner's payer tolerates interruptions.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The checkpoint rules became a 2034 midterm issue in Florida and Arizona House races. AARP backs coverage and opposes the scale requirement. MAHA legislators oppose the rule as overmedication, while some fiscal conservatives back the Texas lawsuit against it. There is still no evidence on turnout effects.

state.regulatory_posture: Expansive on coverage, routine on drugs, still permissive on marketing. FDA approved the AUD indication and the 50 mg parity pill, declined to label reward blunting, and issued a warning letter to Novo over reporting. CMS rewrote the reading of the Part D exclusion by rule. Congress did not legislate. A Loper Bright challenge to the rule (State of Texas et al. and a taxpayer group, N.D. Tex., filed Feb 2034) awaits summary judgment.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Medicare Part D covers obesity treatment from Jan 2034 under a verified-adherence protocol. Medicaid covers AUD use in every state and obesity use in 13, with an enhanced administrative match for states that adopt the protocol. TrumpRx is unchanged.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning is now federal policy. Part D plans mail cellular connected scales to obesity-route enrollees, and continued coverage depends on fill data (proportion of days covered ≥80%) plus weight readings at months 6 and 12. 11 Medicaid states use the same protocol, and several have added app-based counselling attendance for AUD prior authorisation. Employer adherence differentials up to 30% continue under the 2027 guidance; Illinois still bans them. Scale and fill data flow to plan vendors under consent forms bundled with enrolment.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT guidance (Jun 2034) treats AUD-indicated oral semaglutide like naltrexone for commercial drivers: permitted, with documentation in the return-to-duty process. Calm-plan use is unaddressed. TRICARE covers the AUD indication. The Army recruit pilot is unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China still supply about two-thirds of world volume, and Indian generic oral semaglutide wins tenders across Africa and Southeast Asia. The Novo scandal became a Danish domestic issue, with pension-fund exposure debated in the Folketing. US–India mail enforcement talks are still without agreement.

events.event: FDA approves oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder in adults; ASAM lists it as first-line within weeks, and Medicaid programmes must cover it as a medically accepted indication

CMS finalises Part D rule covering obesity drugs from January 2034, conditioning continued coverage on verified fills and connected-scale weigh-ins at six and twelve months; enhanced Medicaid match offered to states adopting the same protocol

Documents unsealed in the EPI litigation show Novo Nordisk held a 2027 internal analysis of falling pancreatic enzyme levels for over two years before reporting; CEO resigns in October, DOJ opens civil probe, FDA warning letter follows in December

FDA Sentinel study confirms dose-related emotional flattening at rates seen in earlier cohorts; agency declines a warning and adds 'mood changes' to counselling materials as clinicians normalise 'drug holidays'
FDA approves Wegovy pill 50 mg with label language showing non-inferiority to injectable Wegovy; Novo lists it at $229 on TrumpRx and Medicare plans make it the default obesity-route product

First Medicare six-month checkpoints remove about 1.2 million obesity-route enrollees for missed fills or missing weigh-ins; CMS adds a prescriber-directed interruption exception code as the Texas suit against the rule proceeds

open_tensions: Medicare is now the largest payer, but the obesity route rests on a CMS reinterpretation of a statutory exclusion under Loper Bright challenge in Texas. If the court strikes it, about 5 million beneficiaries lose coverage at once, and the regain curve is well known.

Verified adherence and drug holidays pull against each other. Clinicians write interruption orders to protect patients' coverage, plans audit those orders, and monthly clinic-shot workers cannot take holidays at all.

The company whose pill is the Medicare default, the AUD standard and the new parity product concealed a known pancreatic finding. The DOJ probe and the 2035 EPI bellwether trials will test how far trust, not data, governs persistence.
Being off now needs explaining just as teen oral use rises, while final adult height for children started before puberty remains unknown until the next analysis in 2035.

prose.headline: The Pill at Breakfast: Medicare Pays, the Scale Reports Back, and Everyone Asks Why You Stopped
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 nearly sixty million American adults, a little over one in five, take an incretin drug, and almost a third have tried one. The bigger change is that being on it no longer means anything. The pill sits beside the coffee in retirement condos in Florida and Arizona, in Louisville apartments, and in the kitchens of salaried couples in Charlotte. What people ask about now is why someone is off it.

The government did most of that. In April 2033 Medicare rewrote its reading of the old law that kept weight-loss drugs out of Part D, and from January 2034 it began paying for obesity treatment. Congress never voted on it. Five million older Americans joined in a year, many moving off the cash channel, and Medicare and Medicaid together now pay for more users than employers do. Coverage came with conditions. Plans mail out a cellular scale that reports weight on its own. Coverage continues only if pharmacy records show at least eighty percent of days covered and the scale shows loss or maintenance at six and twelve months. In August the first checkpoints removed about a million two hundred thousand people. Some went back to cash, some to the mail, some to nothing. Texas and a taxpayer group have sued, arguing the agency had no power to reinterpret the statute, and the case is awaiting a ruling.

The drug also got the new use doctors had expected. In January 2033 oral semaglutide was approved for alcohol use disorder, and because Medicaid must cover approved treatments, a drinker in a state that refuses to pay for weight loss can now get the same pill for drinking. Bourbon makers in Bardstown mothballed lines. The calm-and-focus subscriptions that sold low-dose evenness as a product lost subscribers, and most of the platforms now advertise drinking less.

The pill also caught up with the needle. In March 2034 Novo's 50-milligram Wegovy pill won a label saying it works about as well as the weekly injection, and at $229 a month in the government's cash channel it became the default on Medicare plans. Starter doses are still $149, and the $1,349 list price is still printed on the box. Prices keep falling slowly, set by deals rather than competition, and no American generic exists.

The company that makes that pill spent the year in disgrace. In September 2033 court documents showed Novo had held an internal analysis of declining pancreatic enzyme levels for more than two years before reporting it. The risk was the one already on the label, but the timing was new. The chief executive left, the Justice Department opened an inquiry, the FDA sent a warning letter, and the shares fell by a quarter. Prescriptions kept rising, because Medicare had already chosen the pill.

The flatness became an ordinary complaint. An FDA study in late 2033 found the same dose-related rate of lost pleasure that earlier cohorts had counted, and the agency again declined a warning. People manage it the way they manage caffeine. They step down the dose, or they take a holiday: a weekend off for a wedding, Thanksgiving or an anniversary, when food tastes like something again. That runs straight into the eighty-percent rule, so doctors now write formal interruption orders and Medicare added a code for them. Workers on the monthly plant-clinic shot along the Columbus freight corridor cannot take a holiday at all.

No new safety finding arrived in the window, which is not the same as reassurance. The children who started before puberty are still growing more slowly than expected, and no one will know their adult height for years. Teenagers are starting the pill because everyone else is on it. From a distance the country looks steady, weighed by a scale that reports to the government.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dolores Reyes takes the pill at 6:40 with exactly four ounces of water, then waits thirty minutes before coffee, standing at the sink in her Ocala condo. The scale in the bathroom blinks green. It sent 171 pounds to someone before she had her glasses on.

Her Part D app says 86 percent. Her granddaughter Marisol is getting married in three weeks. Dolores wants Friday through Sunday off so she can taste the tres leches she ordered. She does the arithmetic on a church bulletin: three days off puts her at 81. Close.

At pickleball, Jean asks about her nephew Tony, who is thick again in the face, and Dolores says he lost his job and the Georgia vials made him sick. Jean nods as if that counts as a reason. Bev says her daughter in Columbus can't skip the clinic shot even for a christening. Everyone agrees that's a shame.

The pharmacy copay is forty-seven dollars. The bag has a Novo leaflet inside, and Dolores thinks about the man on the news who resigned, then folds it into the drawer with the others.

At four the doctor's office calls back. Dr. Anand will write the interruption order, code and all, so the weekend won't count against her. The nurse says lots of people are doing it for weddings.

Dinner is half a pork chop and green beans. She is not hungry and has not been hungry since February. She sets the alarm for 6:40, then sits a while in the dark kitchen, trying to remember what she used to want at this hour.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Imported or counterfeit product is ~6.4M (10.7%), down from 7.5M as Medicaid AUD and obesity coverage absorbed part of the bottom third.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the gray market is said to shrink even as ~1.2M people are cut at Medicare checkpoints and sent to cash or the mail. Medicaid obesity coverage reaches only 13 states, and the chain from those states to the bottom third's switching is asserted, not shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Five million older Americans joined in a year, many moving off the cash channel
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and mechanism: the world gives ~5.0M on the obesity route, yet also removes ~1.2M at the August checkpoint. The prose does not say whether 5M is gross or net, and the first-year ramp of ~5M plus mailed cellular scales is aggressive.

least_plausible_claims.quote: She does the arithmetic on a church bulletin: three days off puts her at 81.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a proportion-of-days-covered figure measured over a six-month window would fall only ~1–2 points from three missed days, not five. The prose contradicts the world's own PDC mechanism.

rationale.badness: Federal benefits conditioning (mailed connected scales, PDC ≥80%) removed ~1.2M people at the first checkpoint, creating a visible regain cohort. Added to that are mainstream flatness managed by 'holidays', Novo's concealment scandal, and rising teen oral use with the child growth question unresolved. Offsetting benefits are real: AUD treatment, Medicaid coverage in 13 states and fewer gray-market users soften inequality and public health, so this is a harder society with new losers rather than a structural horror.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and dated events: adoption +2.2pp, managed decline, Medicare/Medicaid expansion, AUD approval, 50 mg pill parity, Novo scandal, normalisation, conditioning, and flatness as a mainstream complaint.
